name: Thomson Reuters Corporation
executive_summary:
Thomson Reuters is a high-quality, subscription-led professional information business (legal, tax, accounting, news) that the quantitative screen rates **Strong Buy**, driven by cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, and risk-factor passes at a sector-relative composite of 77%. The valuation hook is a de-rated franchise trading at roughly 24.7× earnings and 3.1% yield after a sharp share-price reset, with Neff PEGY of 0.08 suggesting growth and income are mispriced relative to fundamentals. The central debate is whether generative AI erodes Thomson Reuters’ moat in legal and tax workflows—or whether proprietary content, compliance embedding, and “AI-as-product” investments turn disruption into an upgrade cycle. Capital return (dividends, buybacks, and a 2026 return-of-capital programme) supports the value case, but filing extracts in this pack are too thin to fully validate reported trends from primary documents alone.

---
investment_thesis:
The screen’s Strong Buy label rests on unusually broad factor confirmation: **10 of 22 models passed**, spanning **cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, and risk** families, with full data quality (20/20 metrics) and building conviction (69%, stable for three weeks). For a value investor, the case is not a deep cyclical discount but a **quality compounder at a cyclically depressed multiple**—P/E 24.7, P/B 3.3, ROE 12.7%, ~3.1% yield, and PEGY 0.08 against ~5.6% growth in the screen snapshot.

Business quality aligns with the factor profile. Thomson Reuters operates mission-critical, recurring-revenue software and content for professionals—segments where switching costs, regulatory relevance, and workflow integration support the **Economic Moat**, **Quality Value**, **Earnings Quality**, and **Piotroski F-Score** passes. Free cash flow of roughly **$1.7bn** (screen) and rising operating cash generation (Yahoo fallback: FCF **$2.02bn** in FY2025) underpin **High Dividend Yield**, **Dividend Growth**, and **Composite Value** signals. The **Dreman Contrarian** and **Magic Formula** passes fit a narrative of market pessimism (AI disruption, post-portfolio-simplification noise) against still-resilient underlying economics.

Portfolio actions—sale of non-core assets, the KKR joint venture for Global Print, and aggressive shareholder returns—have simplified the equity story toward higher-margin recurring revenue, which the screen interprets as undervalued durability rather than structural decline.

financial_review:
### Source hierarchy and gaps

**Primary filings indexed (SEC EDGAR, `regime: sec_edgar`):**
- **Annual:** Form 40-F for years ended **31 Dec 2024** (filed 6 Mar 2025) and **31 Dec 2025** (filed 5 Mar 2026).
- **Interim:** 37 Form 6-K filings, including referenced **Q1 2025**, **H1 2025** (`tri-20250630`), **Q3 2025**, and **Q1 2026** interim reports.

**Critical gap:** Of 39 indexed filings, only **12 have body extracts**, and those bodies are **procedural** (debt exchange, proxy circulars, capital-return notices, indentures)—not earnings releases or financial statements. The 40-F bodies contain exhibit indexes referencing MD&A and audited accounts but **not the numerical content**. Interim earnings bodies for Q1/Q2/Q3 2025 and Q1 2026 are **indexed but not downloaded** (`has_body: false`). **No going-concern, contingency, or covenant language** is available in the body extracts reviewed.

Accordingly, **all quantitative trends below fall back to Yahoo `financials_annual.json`** (and cached quarterly income for Q1 2026), stated explicitly. Figures should be verified against full 40-F exhibits and interim reports before trading.

### Annual trends (Yahoo fallback; USD millions unless noted)

| Metric | FY2022 | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 |
|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|
| Revenue | 6,627 | 6,794 | 7,258 | 7,476 |
| Operating income | 1,815 | 1,950 | 1,896 | 1,989 |
| Net income | 1,338 | 2,695 | 2,210 | 1,502 |
| Diluted EPS ($) | 3.03 | 5.89 | 4.97 | 3.38 |
| EBITDA | 3,010 | 2,950 | 3,052 | 3,047 |
| Free cash flow | 1,320 | 1,797 | 1,850 | 2,017 |

**Revenue** has compounded steadily (+13% from FY2022 to FY2025), consistent with a subscription-led professional information model. **Operating income** is broadly flat-to-up, suggesting core profitability has held despite portfolio reshaping.

**Reported net income and EPS** are volatile: FY2023–FY2024 benefited from large **gain-on-sale** and equity-interest items (e.g. FY2023 gain on sale of business **$384m**; FY2024 **$196m**); FY2025 net income fell as unusual gains moderated (**$92m** other income) and the tax rate normalised (tax provision **$423m** vs **$(123)m** credit in FY2024 per Yahoo). Normalised earnings power is better reflected in **operating income (~$2.0bn)** and **EBITDA (~$3.0bn)** than in headline net income.

**Cash generation is improving:** FCF rose from **$1.32bn** (FY2022) to **$2.02bn** (FY2025); operating cash flow **$2.65bn** in FY2025. Capex remains manageable (**$634m**, ~8.5% of revenue).

### Balance sheet and capital structure (Yahoo fallback, FY2025)

- **Total debt:** $2.37bn; **net debt:** $1.75bn (cash **$371m**).
- **Goodwill and intangibles:** $12.66bn on **$17.94bn** total assets—**tangible book value negative ($856m)**, typical of acquisitive content/software franchises but a screen blind spot.
- **Deferred revenue (current):** $1.25bn—supports recurring-revenue interpretation.
- **Pension/post-retirement obligations (non-current):** **$504m** employee benefits liability.
- **Working capital:** negative **$1.24bn**, largely deferred-revenue driven rather than distress.

**Capital return (FY2025, Yahoo):** common dividends **$1.04bn**; share repurchases **$1.0bn**; long-term debt repayments **$1.06bn**. Filing index corroborates active debt management: multiple **6-K debt exchange offers and indenture amendments** (Feb–Mar 2025).

### Interim / recent quarter (Yahoo quarterly fallback; filing bodies absent)

**Q1 2026** (period in Yahoo cache): revenue **$2,087m** vs **$1,785m** in Q1 2025 (+~17% YoY); operating income **$636m** vs **$443m**; diluted EPS **$1.05** vs **$0.70**; net income **$459m**. This suggests **accelerating top-line and margin improvement** in the most recent reported quarter, but the corresponding **Q1 2026 interim report body is not in the pack**—treat as indicative only.

### Filing-corroborated non-financial items (primary sources)

From 6-K exhibit descriptions (bodies only):
- **25 Feb 2026:** new **US$600m share repurchase programme** and **US$605m return of capital and share consolidation** (Material Change Report filed).
- **Mar 2025:** debt exchange offers, consent solicitations, and replacement indentures—balance-sheet refinancing activity, not distress signals in available text.
- **6 Mar 2025 / 5 Mar 2026:** annual 40-F filings for FY2024 and FY2025—financial statements **not extracted** in bodies.

risks_and_flags:
**AI disruption (primary market concern).** News flow repeatedly flags AI as re-pricing the legal/tax research moat (e.g. “Barclays Cuts Thomson Reuters (TRI) Target, Says AI Narrative Still Dominates”, 13 Apr 2025; “UBS Trims … Wells Fargo Stays Neutral on AI Concerns”, 26 Apr 2025). If AI commoditises research retrieval, pricing power and retention in Legal Professionals and Tax & Accounting could erode faster than screens capture.

**Intangibles-heavy balance sheet.** Goodwill and intangibles exceed **70%** of total assets; tangible book is **negative**. Impairment or slower amortisation benefit would hit perceived asset backing and P/B-oriented value models.

**Earnings quality and one-offs.** Reported net income is heavily influenced by divestiture gains, equity-method swings, and tax items (Yahoo fallback). FY2025 continuing net income **$1.48bn** vs total **$1.50bn**—smaller gap than prior years, but screens using trailing EPS may still embed non-recurring history.

**Pension and employee liabilities.** **$504m** non-current employee benefit obligations (Yahoo, FY2025)—material but not screened as a primary risk factor here; full 40-F note disclosure unavailable in body extracts.

**Governance structure.** The **Founders Share Company** (Woodbridge) controls a special share with strategic influence; **Kim Williams retirement** and appointment of **Dr. Stephen J. Toope** as chairman (13 Jan 2026) is a governance transition worth monitoring. Shareholder proposal rejected and two new directors added (11 Jun 2025) suggest active but not fully aligned investor debate.

**Operational restructuring.** Reuters reported a **“small number” of engineering job cuts** (13 Jul 2025) amid AI/product realignment—cost saves possible, execution risk on product roadmap.

**Debt and refinancing.** Mar 2025 exchange offers and multiple supplemental indentures indicate active capital-markets activity. Without covenant text in bodies, leverage appears moderate (**net debt/EBITDA ~0.6×** on Yahoo EBITDA), but refinancing terms are unverified in this pack.

**Filing-data gap itself.** Inability to read MD&A risk factors, contingencies, or going-concern language from primary bodies is a **research red flag**—not a company red flag, but it limits conviction on legal/regulatory exposures.
